public_rationale: Marcus's $500,000 figure matches MosaicML's September 2022 estimate of about $450K for a GPT-3-quality model. Within six months of the post the price had fallen well below that. In May 2023 MosaicML reported training MPT-7B from scratch for about $200k. In June 2023 it released MPT-30B, an open model it says beats the original GPT-3, and said anyone could fully fine-tune it into their own custom model for a few hundred dollars. Any ordinary reading of 'soon' covers six months. The result does depend on counting fine-tuning as 'custom-trained', or on accepting a smaller model.
limitations: The figures are MosaicML's own and depend on its GPU pricing.
The from-scratch MPT-7B model is smaller than GPT-3 class, and the far cheaper figure is for fine-tuning rather than training from scratch.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The price of a custom-trained large language model (currently under $500,000) will soon drop further.

statement.excerpt: Soon the price will drop further.

from_speaker: your own custom-trained large language model, for keeps
Soon the price will drop further
our_interpretation: The $500,000 baseline matches MosaicML's September 2022 estimate of about $450K to train a GPT-3-quality model. I read the forecast as: soon after December 2022, a person could get their own trained LLM of similar quality, with weights they keep, for clearly less than that.
'Soon' has no fixed date. I treat it as roughly within two years of the post, and settle it early only through a dated, documented price.
I count both training from scratch and fine-tuning an open model on your own data as 'custom-trained', since in both cases you own the resulting weights.
criteria.support_condition: A dated, documented price or cost, published soon after December 2022, under which a comparable custom LLM with owned weights could be obtained for clearly less than about $450-500K.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Documented costs for a comparable owned custom LLM stayed at or above about $450-500K for the two years after the post.
